requirements: A developer-facing tool — StackShare's ~148k-tool catalog covers languages, frameworks, dev tools, infrastructure, and SaaS used in software stacks
If a page for the tool already exists, click 'Claim This Tool' — verification via official-domain email or the tool's GitHub repo
If no page exists, use the 'List a Tool' flow: name, live public URL, tagline, short description, category; logo optional but recommended
New listings go through a review/categorization step before publishing
preparation: Tool name, live URL, one-line tagline, short description, logo
Decide the right category/tier (Application & Data, Utilities, DevOps, Business Tools, AI)
Verification route: official-domain email or GitHub repo access
Bonus: create your company's public stack and Stack Decisions to give the tool authentic usage signal
workflow: Search for the tool — if a page exists, 'Claim This Tool' and verify ownership (domain email or GitHub)
Otherwise use 'List a Tool' and submit name/URL/tagline/description/category
Once live, the tool page accrues followers, votes, and 'used in stack' citations as companies add it to public stacks
watchFor: Claiming an existing auto-generated page is usually faster than creating a fresh listing
StackShare's value is social proof — a bare listing with no stacks citing it is weak; get your own company stack public first
Invited teammates get FULL permissions on the company profile — invite carefully
